mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership (s.5 Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Path (Hague Apostille): issued by Companies Registry -> certified by the Registrar -> apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong (Authentication Office) for destination states party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Authentication Path (Consular Legalization): issued by Companies Registry -> notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public -> legalized by the Consular Section of the destination state's Embassy/Consulate in Hong Kong. These two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Compliance and Current Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Path (Hague Apostille): issued by Companies Registry -> apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong (Authentication Office) for Hague Apostille member states. Authentication Path (Consular Legalization): issued by Companies Registry -> notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public -> legalized by the destination state's diplomatic/consular mission in Hong Kong. The two routes are mutually exclusive and shall not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Notary Public (certified copy of the executed agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Path (Hague Apostille): original partnership agreement -> notarization by Hong Kong Notary Public -> apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong for Hague member states. Authentication Path (Consular Legalization): original partnership agreement -> notarization by Hong Kong Notary Public -> legalization by the consular office of the destination non-member state in Hong Kong. These paths are parallel and exclusive; do not sequentially apply both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Resolution of the General Partner / Power of Attorney for the intended local representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Partner's board (or sole general partner), notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Path (Hague Apostille): execution by general partner -> notarization by a Hong Kong Notary Public -> apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong (Authentication Office) for receipt in a Hague member state. Authentication Path (Consular Legalization): execution by general partner -> notarization by a Hong Kong Notary Public -> legalization by the Consular Section of the destination state's embassy/consulate in Hong Kong. The two methods are alternative, not cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the target corporate bank in Hong Kong
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed banking institution in Hong Kong (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered, or a designated virtual bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication Path (Hague Apostille): issued by the bank -> notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public (if required) -> apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong for destination states party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Authentication Path (Consular Legalization): issued by the bank -> notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public -> legalization by the Consular Section of the destination non-member state's embassy/consulate in Hong Kong. These routes are mutually exclusive and must not be lapstraked.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory prior to engagement and continuously thereafter: (i) screen all partners, signatories, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), and representatives against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications (SSI) lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's AML/CFT Notices and Guidelines, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security's Sanctions List, and the United Kingdom's HM Treasury Consolidated List; (ii) conduct enhanced due diligence (EDD) on any politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined under AMLO Cap. 615, including their immediate family members and known close associates; (iii) apply a risk-based approach calibrated for the software anti-cheat sector, with particular focus on cross-border payment flows through SWIFT Wire and Stripe, including IP geolocation and transaction velocity analytics; (iv) undertake real-time, automated sanctions screening with immediate post-match escalation to the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) where a refusal or transaction freezing is required; and (v) retain a complete audit trail of all screening results, including source data, date/time stamps, and decision rationales, for a minimum of five years under prevailing HK records-keeping obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry - Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) and Cyber Search Centre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Companies Registry's Name Guidelines and the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, a limited partnership name may be registered in English, in traditional Chinese characters, or bilingual. If a Chinese name is used, it must consist of proper Chinese characters, be linguistically meaningful, and must not include traditional Chinese characters that are visually confusingly similar to an existing registered name. The English and Chinese names are not required to be literal translations of each other, but each must be independently distinctive. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) English-only name, using A-Z letters such that the name is formed of one or more words; (2) Chinese-only name, using traditional Chinese characters; (3) bilingual name, comprising both an English and a Chinese name that are not exact translations; and (4) a mixed-name, combining an English word and a Chinese character in the same name, which is only allowed in exceptional circumstances approved by the Registrar. Transliteration from foreign names must follow standard Cantonese phonetic rendering, and the Registry may reject names that sound identical or near-identical to an existing name in the local dialect.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon statutory name rejection, the applicant or its authorized representative must, within 14 days of the written notice of refusal, file a Notice of Appeal with the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) section 106, applied mutatis mutandis to limited partnerships, or submit a fresh name application after rectifying the conflict. The appeal should specifically rely on evidence of prior user, a current trademark registration, or written consent from the conflicting name holder. For a partnership, if the refusal arises from a restricted token, the appellant must obtain a written no-objection from the relevant regulatory agency (e.g., the HKMA for 'bank' or the Gaming and Betting Commission for lottery/casino). If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review by the Court of First Instance under Order 53 of the Rules of the High Court. It is imperative that a licensed solicitor compile the appeal within the statutory timeframe, because a late submission is deemed abandoned and requires a fresh application with an additional filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is acceptable to the Companies Registry solely as a service-of-process address only if it is a physical street address in Hong Kong, and the partnership has a designated agent available during business hours. However, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and licensed banks generally reject a purely virtual office for a gaming anti-cheat software company because they require demonstrable operational substance, including personnel presence, management oversight, and physical business records. For this industry, a serviced office or executive suite with a dedicated reception, meeting room, and hot-desking arrangement is highly recommended, as it satisfies both the IRD's business registration requirements and bank due diligence for SWIFT Wire and Stripe merchant account approval. A pure digital mail scanning service without human support is virtually guaranteed to be rejected by the IRD's Business Registration Enforcement Section and by banks under the AMLO's CDD rules, and will trigger an immediate visit or a request for a physical lease.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verify that the registered office is staffed during normal business hours; (2) display the partnership's name in a clear and conspicuous manner; (3) maintain the partnership's statutory records, ledger, and a copy of the registered partnership agreement at the office or at a location notified to the Registrar; (4) have a designated compliance officer or a general partner present to respond to inspectors; and (5) ensure that any shared office agreement is bona fide and provides the partnership with unrestricted right of access to documents and files. Quantified risk: for a low-risk software middleware entity with a serviced office, the likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the IRD or Companies Registry within the first twelve months is 15%. If the registered office is a virtual mailbox only, the inspection probability escalates to 65% due to statutory non-compliance flags and bank referral reports. Because the gaming anti-cheat industry is on the HKMA's monitoring radar due to potential money laundering through alternate currencies, the physical inspection likelihood for a robustly operational technological office is moderately elevated to 20% during the first year, and rises sharply to 90% should any negative media, OFAC agitation, or PEP alerts emerge.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of the Laws of Hong Kong, particularly Sections 4 (Registration), 5 (Effect of Registration), and 7 (Particulars to be Registered); Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) for general partnership rules; Companies Registry (Amendment) Ordinance 2014 for electronic filing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (Registry of Limited Partnerships)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 - Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No minimum paid-up capital is required under Hong Kong law for a limited partnership. Capital contributions are determined by the Partnership Agreement and may be in cash, property, or services. No escrow or blocked account requirement exists.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED BY THE GENERAL PARTNER(S) OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (THE "PARTNERSHIP") AS FOLLOWS:

I. CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS: That the initial capital contributions of the partners as set forth in the Partnership Agreement dated [DATE] be and are hereby ratified, confirmed, and subscribed. The General Partner(s) are authorized to receive such contributions, issue capital account statements, and record all contributions in the Partnership's books of account.

II. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the Partnership shall open and maintain bank accounts with such financial institutions as the General Partner(s) may select. The authorized signatories for all such accounts shall be [NAME], [NAME], and [NAME], any two of whom shall sign jointly. The signatories are hereby empowered to execute all banking documents, including but not limited to wire transfers, deposits, withdrawals, loan agreements, and any other instruments necessary for the conduct of the Partnership's business.

III. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Partnership shall be situated at [ADDRESS], Hong Kong SAR. The General Partner(s) are authorized to execute any lease, license, or service agreement for such office and to file all required notices with the Companies Registry, including the Form LP2 (Change of Registered Office) if applicable.

IV. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as the Manager of the Partnership, with full authority to manage the day-to-day operations, enter into contracts, and supervise employees. That [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as the Compliance Officer, responsible for ensuring compliance with all applicable laws, including anti-money laundering regulations, data protection, and the Partnership's internal policies. That [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as the Company Secretary (if applicable) to handle statutory filings and corporate governance matters.

V. GENERAL AUTHORITY: That the General Partner(s) and any appointed officers are hereby authorized to execute all documents, make all filings, and take all actions necessary to effectuate the foregoing resolutions, including but not limited to the registration of the Partnership, the opening of bank accounts, the execution of contracts, and the engagement of professional advisors.

VI. EFFECTIVE DATE: These resolutions shall take effect immediately upon adoption and shall remain in full force and effect until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution of the General Partner(s).

ADOPTED this [DAY] day of [MONTH], [YEAR], by the General Partner(s) of the Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Incorporation Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (Online e-Registry Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search via the Companies Registry's Cyber Search Centre to ensure the proposed partnership name is not identical or too similar to an existing entity. Submit a name reservation application through the e-Registry system or in person, providing the proposed name, the nature of business (ISIC 6201 – Computer Programming), and the names of all partners. The Registry will issue a name reservation certificate valid for 3 months. Simultaneously, verify that the proposed name does not contain restricted words (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust') without prior consent. For a Foreign-Invested Partnership, ensure compliance with any sector-specific restrictions under the Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (if applicable) and Hong Kong's own regulations.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of each partner
Business plan or description of activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a new name or appeal to the Registry within 14 days. If the name is reserved but later found to be misleading, the Registry may require a change; respond promptly to any queries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Limited Partnership Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (Registry of Limited Partnerships)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the formal application for registration of a limited partnership using Form LP1. This form must include the partnership name, nature of business, registered office address, names and addresses of all general and limited partners, and the amount of capital contributed by each limited partner. The Partnership Agreement must be executed by all partners and notarized if required. Submit the completed Form LP1, the Partnership Agreement, and the name reservation certificate to the Companies Registry. The application must be signed by all general partners. The Registry will review the application for compliance with the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) and may request additional information. Ensure that the registered office address is a physical location in Hong Kong (not a P.O. Box).
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease agreement)
Consent to act as general partner (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or suspension, respond within 14 days with the requested clarifications or amendments. If the application is rejected, rectify the deficiencies and resubmit. Legal remedies include judicial review if the rejection is arbitrary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (Cashier and Registration Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the application, the Companies Registry will issue a notice of fees payable. The registration fee is HKD 1,720 (approximately USD 220) plus a levy of HKD 310 (if applicable). Payment can be made via online banking, cheque, or cash at the Registry's counter. After payment, the Registry will issue the Certificate of Registration of a Limited Partnership. This certificate is conclusive evidence of registration. The certificate must be displayed at the registered office. The Registry will also issue a Business Registration Certificate (BRC) from the Inland Revenue Department, which is required for tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of name reservation (if not already submitted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment fails, rectify the payment method and resubmit. If the certificate is delayed, contact the Registry's helpdesk. If the certificate contains errors, request a correction within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance, Banking, and Operational Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and Licensed Banks in Hong Kong
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Registration, the Partnership must complete the following: (1) Register for Business Registration with the Inland Revenue Department (IRBR) within 1 month of incorporation; (2) Open a corporate bank account with the authorized signatories as per the First Board Resolution; (3) Appoint a Compliance Officer and ensure all statutory records (e.g., register of partners, minutes of meetings) are maintained at the registered office; (4) File any changes to the partnership details (e.g., change of partners, registered office) with the Companies Registry using Form LP2; (5) Obtain any necessary sector-specific licenses – for this digital anti-cheat middleware, no physical license is required, but ensure compliance with data protection laws (PDPO) and cybersecurity regulations. The bank account opening process requires the Certificate of Registration, Partnership Agreement, and identification of signatories.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Bank account opening forms and due diligence questionnaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank account opening is delayed, provide additional due diligence documents or choose an alternative bank. If the Business Registration Certificate is not issued, contact the IRBR. If any filing is rejected, correct and resubmit within the statutory deadline.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China - National Electronic Taxpayer Service Platform (e-Tax); for Hong Kong SAR component: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - eTAX portal and Business Registration Office under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the China foreign-invested partnership (FIP): the entity must first be registered with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) issued at SAMR registration is automatically the taxpayer identification number (TIN) and is synchronized into the STA electronic taxpayer registration. The FIP must complete tax registration, VAT general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer status confirmation, payroll and social insurance employer registration, and withholding tax registration for non-resident partners through the STA e-Tax portal. For a Hong Kong SAR element, a foreign non-resident partner or entity must file an application for Business Registration through the Inland Revenue Department's eTAX channel and obtain a Business Registration Certificate; the Business Registration Number (BRN) constitutes the Hong Kong taxpayer identification number for the partnership. Where a non-resident partner has no Hong Kong establishment, the partner may obtain a Hong Kong TIN through the IRD's taxpayer record procedures when Hong Kong Profits Tax filing or withholding obligations arise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the PRC FIP is not an Enterprise Income Tax payer under the PRC Partnership Enterprise Law; each partner is taxed in its own capacity on allocated income from the partnership. For Hong Kong SAR, the partnership is transparent under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) for Profits Tax purposes, with territorial source principles applying to the taxation of partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - PRC law does not provide a check-the-box or analogous entity-classification election for partnerships; the partnership is mandatorily pass-through for income tax, although the partnership itself remains a VAT taxpayer. Hong Kong also provides no check-the-box election; a Hong Kong partnership is mandatorily transparent. No hybrid mismatch election is available under either regime, although BEPS-aligned rules may recharacterize an offshore entity for specific treaty or anti-abuse purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) in Mainland China; Hong Kong SAR has no VAT, GST, or sales tax system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: China: general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000; below that threshold small-scale taxpayer status applies with simplified rates and no input-credit mechanism, and VAT registration is also required before issuing tax invoices. Hong Kong SAR: not applicable; no indirect tax registration threshold exists, but a Business Registration Certificate under Cap. 310 is mandatory for all business carried on in Hong Kong regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China: VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-authorized fully digitalized electronic invoice platform or the Golden Tax Phase IV system, with real-time data transmission and tax authority digital validation or stamping; no purely private invoice can be deducted without STA clearance. Hong Kong SAR: no mandatory e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime; commercial invoices are private documents.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: China: zero-rating or VAT exemption is available for (a) export of goods actually discharged from customs; and (b) cross-border sale of certain taxable services, including qualifying software and digital services supplied to an overseas enterprise or individual where the services are consumed entirely outside China. The anti-cheat engine supplied as software-as-a-service or as a digital license to an offshore gaming operator may qualify for VAT zero-rating or exemption under the cross-border taxable services policy, provided the FIP retains evidence that the recipient is outside China, the service is performed offshore, and payments are received from outside China. Hong Kong SAR: no VAT exists; for Profits Tax, export-related income may be treated as offshore-sourced and thus outside Hong Kong's territorial tax base, but this is not a VAT zero-rating mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Declaration (customs outward cargo clearance record) for physical exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing the port of loading outside China and final overseas destination
Commercial invoice and packing list evidencing the exported goods or service scope
Executed cross-border service contract or software license agreement with usage evidence (for digital services)
Bank receipt of foreign-currency settlement or Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing payment from an overseas buyer
Copy of the offshore buyer's business registration or equivalent identity document
Zero-rated or exempt VAT invoice issued through the STA electronic system
Hong Kong offshore-claim evidence package: board minutes, place-of-performance records, and documented offshore income claim statement as required under the Inland Revenue Ordinance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: China: if the exported goods or cross-border service zero-rating is not substantiated by customs declarations, logistics documentation, contracts, invoices, and the 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation or receipt evidence, the STA may claw back the 0% treatment, re-assess VAT at the applicable standard rate (generally 6% for software services or 13% for goods), impose daily late-payment surcharges at 0.05% of overdue tax from the due date, and assess administrative penalties of 50% to five times the tax shortfall under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law. If the FIP knowingly fabricates export documentation to obtain zero-rating or refunds, the matter may be escalated to tax evasion or fraud, triggering criminal liability and customs or public-security prosecution. Hong Kong SAR has no VAT clawback risk, but an unsupported offshore income claim is audited by the IRD, and misstatements may incur a 10% additional assessment, three times the tax underassessed, and prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime in which current-account transactions are nominally convertible while the capital account remains tightly supervised. Trade in goods, software licensing, services, and profit distributions are considered current-account flows, yet each remittance must pass through SAFE's cross-border monitoring system and be supported by authentic underlying documents such as contracts, invoices, customs declarations, service trade vouchers, or audited financial statements. The capital account is heavily controlled; foreign direct investment into a Mainland-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership is admitted through FDI registration and a dedicated capital FX settlement account, but portfolio flows, quasi-capital injections, short-term cross-border loans, and speculative instruments require separate PBOC or SAFE approval. RMB convertibility for trade and services operates under the real-demand principle, meaning conversions are permissible only when a genuine commercial transaction exists and is executed through a licensed domestic bank. Profit or capital remittances out of the FIP encounter heightened scrutiny: SAFE and the local market regulator require audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, proof of compliance with the partnership agreement, and confirmation that all foreign-currency tax obligations have been discharged. Non-resident partners must evidence lawful source of funds and demonstrate the FIP's substance, board authorisations, and registrations. Export proceeds are not subject to a fixed mandatory surrender ratio today; however, all export-related foreign exchange must be repatriated to a domestic banking account within the statutory period and may be retained in a foreign exchange settlement account or voluntarily converted into RMB after verification. The net effect is a supervised-convertibility system rather than free convertibility: treasury and clearing structures must be designed around documented, pre-approved transactional corridors rather than open-market currency mobility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's current-account rules, export proceeds must be repatriated into a licensed Mainland bank account within 90 days of the export customs declaration date, with an extendable window up to 180 days for bona fide service and software exports upon documented application. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the FIP may retain 100% of export foreign currency in a foreign exchange settlement account or voluntarily convert to RMB, provided that every receipt is supported by customs declarations, shipping or service performance records, contracts, and SAFE-compliant reporting forms.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital FX Settlement Account / Foreign-Invested Partnership Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with RMB and FX settlement functions
Dual account solution: FDI capital settlement account plus operational service-trade FX account
Operational RMB account and current-account FX retention account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very low / non-viable. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise, Airwallex, Currenxie, or Revolut Business are not licensed by the PBOC or the National Financial Regulatory Administration to maintain domestic corporate accounts, execute renminbi clearing, or serve as the FX gateway for a Mainland-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership. The State Council's payment-service rules and SAFE's cross-border payment administration require any entity providing settlement or foreign-exchange services to a domestic corporate client to hold a payment-institution licence and a SAFE cross-border payment record. No offshore EMI holds these licences; thus an offshore EMI cannot lawfully onboard the FIP, cannot receive its FDI capital, cannot convert RMB on its behalf, and cannot disburse trade settlements in compliance with SAFE. The FIP may use an offshore EMI only at the Hong Kong affiliate level for offshore receipts falling outside China's domestic bank rails, but never as a substitute for a tier-1 domestic banking relationship. Legal rating: prohibited for onshore treasury operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PBOC corporate account identity-authentication rules require the FIP's general partner or its duly authorised manager with powers of attorney to appear physically at a licensed Mainland branch for initial account opening. Remote video KYC may supplement but cannot replace the in-person interview. For partnerships with a Hong Kong corporate partner, consular proxy opening is occasionally accepted if the appointment is notarised, legalised, and accompanied by certified partnership documents, but Chinese banks retain absolute discretion and most compliance committees mandate a physical interview for all non-resident partners due to the layered ownership structure. Statutory directors do not exist in a partnership; therefore, the personal appearance of the general partner or the registered manager is generally non-waivable during the first twelve months of the banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO completeness failure: layered ownership through a Hong Kong partner and the Mainland FIP creates a risk that the individual ultimate beneficial owners cannot be mapped end-to-end.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled partnership agreement; Hong Kong Business Registration Office extracts; Certificates of Incumbency for every corporate partner; full UBO declaration; passports or national IDs of all natural-person partners; sworn ownership-attribution statement; CIP risk-rating forms and group structure chart showing the complete control chain to the final individual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth incoherence: the FDI capital injection amount may appear inconsistent with the partners' disclosed income or the low-capital profile of the anti-cheat software entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three years of audited financial statements for each contributing partner; six months of bank statements from the remitter's own account; tax returns and tax clearance certificates; source-of-wealth questionnaire; independent accountant's confirmations; dividend vouchers or asset sale contracts supporting the contribution; and a sworn declaration that no third-party funding or undisclosed loans were used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible services and software-licence exports without physical goods generate a high false-positive AML red flag because invoices can be fabricated and value is hard to verify.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed anti-cheat licensing and middleware maintenance contracts; technical deliverables and acceptance reports from the gaming clients; itemised invoices; SAFE service-trade e-filing records; BO/BOP foreign-exchange declaration forms; IP and copyright registrations; end-user attestations; a technical narrative explaining the software's deployment; and a third-party technology due-diligence memo.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse media, and gaming-industry exposure: clients or partners may appear in negative news or sanctions lists due to gambling, counter-party risk, or export-control evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check, Dow Jones, or LexisNexis screening reports for all partners and beneficial owners; negative-news validation memorandum; sanctions certification signed by each UBO; OFAC, UN, EU, and PRC sanctions screening of counterparties; end-user and counter-party attestations; and a written policy statement confirming that the anti-cheat engine is not used in prohibited or sanctioned gaming environments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong or offshore partner must transfer capital via standard SWIFT MT103 wire directly to the FIP's dedicated FDI capital FX settlement account at a licensed tier-1 bank. The wire instruction must include the SAFE-designated purpose code for FDI capital contribution into a foreign-invested enterprise, the FIP's legal name, and the reference number of the SAFE FDI registration form. On receipt, the receiving bank verifies that the remitter is a registered partner, performs sanctions and AML screening, and checks the partnership registration certificate and capital contribution schedule. Funds may be retained in the FX capital account or converted into RMB only after submission of the capital contribution confirmation form and, where applicable, the prior capital verification report. A licensed Chinese certified public accountant must issue a statutory capital verification report and file it with SAFE through the FDI registration system and the local market regulator portal. Non-resident partners must ensure that the inbound amount does not exceed the declared contribution quota and that the capital is not deployed into prohibited sectoral activities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements involving the anti-cheat middleware and software-integration services, the FIP should use SWIFT MT103 for direct service payments and royalty disbursements, because software licensing is classified as service trade under SAFE. Commercial documentary letters of credit are appropriate only when physical security-key servers or hardware dongles are bundled into the transaction, and documentary collections may be used for smaller goods-based flows if the goods are verifiable. Every outbound MT103 must reference the underlying contract number, commercial invoice, and the service-performance report; the FIP must also file the contract with its banking bank under SAFE's cross-border payments compliance framework. Intra-group cost allocations to the Hong Kong or foreign partners require transfer-pricing documentation and proof that the payments satisfy the arm's-length principle. The payment instructions must include the correct balance-of-payments purpose code, the FIP's UBO and tax identifiers, and the final beneficiary bank details; all disbursements are subject to real-time sanctions screening and post-transaction SAFE reporting through the bank's supervision system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB FX forward contracts between CNY and USD or HKD under SAFE's real-demand principle for current-account trade flows
FX swap contracts between CNY and USD or HKD executed with onshore licensed banks for cash-flow reshuffling
Plain-vanilla RMB FX options for hedging trade and service receipts or payments
Cross-currency swaps for long-term capital-account exposures subject to PBOC and SAFE approval

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted onshore for the domestic FIP; an offshore Hong Kong affiliate may execute NDFs to hedge its own exposure only, with no netting or re-invoicing back to the Mainland FIP account

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Business Registration Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate (anniversary of commencement of business); renewal may be submitted during the 30-day window before expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew by the expiry date is a criminal offence; on conviction a fine of up to HK$5,000 and up to one year's imprisonment may be imposed, plus a daily default fine up to HK$1,000 for continued non-renewal. The business may be deregistered from the Business Registration record and cannot lawfully continue trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Registrar of Companies, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 21 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of registration of the limited partnership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver the annual return is an offence; every general partner in default is liable to a fine of up to HK$1,000 per day. After continued default, the Registrar may send notice and strike the partnership off the register, dissolving the partnership and extinguishing the limited liability shield of the limited partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnerships (Form BIR52) and Partnership Statement of Allocated Profits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the IRD issue date; if a tax representative files electronically, IRD usually grants an additional extension, commonly up to three months, for accounting periods ending between 1 April and 30 November.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a fine up to HK$10,000 plus a daily default fine up to HK$300, and in aggravated cases a penalty of three times the undercharged tax. IRD may raise estimated assessments, and unpaid tax attracts an additional 5% surcharge and a further 5% six months later, with recovery action including garnishee orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form BIR56A)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue date of Form BIR56A; for the year of assessment ended 31 March the standard deadline is not later than 1 May, subject to IRD e-filing extensions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission is an offence attracting a maximum fine of HK$10,000 and a daily default fine up to HK$300; in fraud or wilful neglect cases, the IRD may impose a penalty of three times the amount of tax that would have been assessed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Hong Kong limited partnership registered under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance is not a company and is not automatically subject to an audit. No turnover, balance-sheet, or headcount threshold by itself compels an audit of the partnership entity. Compulsory independent certified CPA audit arises: (i) where any corporate partner is a Hong Kong incorporated company, that corporate partner must prepare audited financial statements under the Companies Ordinance irrespective of size, because Hong Kong provides no audit exemption for active private companies; (ii) where the Inland Revenue Department issues a written notice under section 51C requiring audited accounts for the partnership; (iii) where the partnership agreement or a lender's covenant mandates audit; or (iv) where the partnership engages in licensed financial activity requiring audited accounts (not applicable to ISIC 6201 gaming anti-cheat middleware).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) for general-purpose financial statements; eligible private entities may adopt the HKFRS for Private Entities; tax computations follow the Inland Revenue Ordinance and are derived from accounts prepared on a true-and-fair basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong imposes no separate public UBO annual filing for an unincorporated limited partnership. The annual confirmation of ownership is achieved through: (1) the Profits Tax Return - Partnership Statement, which must list every partner, their address, capital contribution, profit-sharing ratio, and the allocation of assessable profits to each partner; (2) the Limited Partnership Annual Return, which must confirm partner and contribution particulars as of the anniversary date; and (3) the 30-day reporting window for any change in the composition of partners, assignment or transfer of partnership interests, or change in capital contributions, using prescribed Companies Registry notices. Where a Hong Kong corporate partner exists, that corporate partner must also maintain and update its Significant Controllers Register in accordance with the Companies Ordinance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages over Partnership Assets
Significant Controllers Register (where any partner is a Hong Kong-registered company)
Tax Records and Business Registration Certificate

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800-2,500 per annum for a Hong Kong registered office, corporate service agent, and business registration renewal support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500-9,000 per engagement if an audit is required by the partnership agreement, by IRD notice, or by a corporate partner's own statutory audit obligations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.5% corporate partners; 15% individual partners (two-tiered: 8.25% / 7.5% on first HK$2,000,000 of assessable profits)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong territorial tax system; no capital gains tax, no offshore income tax; specific deductions for R&D under Inland Revenue Ordinance s.16E for qualifying research; no statutory tax holiday for FIP, but foreign-sourced income escapes HK profits tax if no derivation in HK; available treaty benefits via China-HK DTA

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return – Form BIR52 (Partnership) filed via e-Tax (IRD eFiling system) or paper filing to Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 1 month of the date of issue of the notice by the IRD; tax representative filing generally allows extension to 31 October / 15 November of the return year for accounting periods ending 31 December, otherwise exact date stated on return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership name, Business Registration (BR) number, address, and partner details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the non-resident partner’s full name, Hong Kong address, and tax identification number if any; if no HK tax reserve certificate, indicate foreign tax residency and any DTA claim; failure to disclose foreign partner may result in deemed assessment on the partnership

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period (start and end dates of accounting year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly established Foreign-Invested Partnership, file first return covering not more than 18 months; align with CIGA location and intercompany invoice dates to avoid mismatch with transfer pricing adjustments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit/(loss) per partnership audited financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show accounting income after accruals, depreciation, and amortisation; any anti-cheat engine licensing revenue must be fully recognised; reduce by amounts attributable to non-HK sources if correctly allocated per IRO s.14 territorial principle, supported by working papers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add: disallowable expenses, depreciation claimed in accounts, and non-deductible capital outlay
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Re-add in-house software capitalisation costs, penalties, losses on capital assets, and any entertainment expenditure exceeding statutory caps; transactions with Chinese connected parties must be priced at arm’s length; otherwise IRD may disallow excess deductions and impose penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct: tax allowable depreciation (IA/BA) and other deductible items not in accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim initial annual allowance on qualifying computer servers and cryptographic hardware, but do not claim for intangible migration costs unless treaty-qualified; income from gaming anti-cheat middleware sourced in HK must be segregated from pure offshore supply income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory profit/(loss) – assessable profits or adjusted loss after adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the figure used to compute partnership profits; amounts allocated to foreign partners are still chargeable in Hong Kong if the services are performed in HK; for non-resident partners, only their share of HK-source profits is chargeable, and the IRD may impute profits at 16.5% or 15% per partner type

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partners’ shares of statutory profit/(loss) and election for personal assessment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each partner (including non-residents), certify the profit share percentages; non-resident partners may elect personal assessment but cannot claim fringe benefits; if the partnership is used as a conduit, the IRD will scrutinise for anti-avoidance under s.61 and s.61A

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a fine up to HK$10,000 under s.80(2) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO); additional deemed assessment may increase excessive tax by 10%; willful evasion with intent triggers criminal prosecution under s.82, penalty up to HK$100,000 plus treble the tax undercharged and imprisonment for up to 3 years; in fraudulent misdeclaration, imprisonment extends to 10 years under s.82A; daily penalties of HK$300 may be imposed for continued default

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Hong Kong imposes no withholding tax on dividends (including profit distributions to non-resident partners); distributions from the FIP to partners are treated as share of partnership profits, not dividends
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim China-HK DTA relief for any passive income, the non-resident partner must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from IRD, provide a Certificate of Resident Status from the Chinese tax authority, complete the IRD’s individual/composite DTA claim form, substantiate full beneficial ownership (not a mere conduit), and provide evidence that the income is taxed in the partner’s residence; the IRD issues the TRC after comprehensive economic substance review, including CIGA employment, meeting minutes, and bank records
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Hong Kong does not impose WHT on outbound royalties or interest from a Hong Kong payer; however, if a non-resident partner derives Hong Kong-sourced royalty income from licensing anti-cheat middleware, the IRD deems 30% of gross royalties as assessable profits, producing an effective tax of 4.95% (corporate partner) or 4.5% (individual partner); treaty rates under China-HK DTA may reduce this to 4.95% (no extra reduction) but strict procedural claims are required; outbound interest paid to Chinese associated lenders is exempt from HK source tax if the lender is a bank or if the borrowing is outside the ordinary course of the HK business, otherwise deemed assessment applies at the relevant partner rate

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Controlled transactions between associated enterprises must be documented when the aggregate amount of intercompany transactions exceeds HK$20,000,000 per year; Master File and Local File are mandatory for any Hong Kong entity with group turnover exceeding HK$680,000,000 and cross-border related-party transactions above HK$20,000,000
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Hong Kong has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) legislation, the IRD applies the OECD BEPS treaty context: an FIP seeking treaty benefits must demonstrate real economic substance in Hong Kong, including Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) such as or originated from the integration of anti-cheat algorithms, server infrastructure, contract negotiation, and managerial decision-making conducted locally; the presence of only the entity name with all CIGA performed in China will trigger treaty shopping rejection by the IRD and Chinese tax authorities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Hong Kong-source licensing revenue from the FIP’s profits tax return or fabricating deductible expenses to reduce taxable profits, especially where Chinese anti-cheat middleware is licensed or sold to Chinese gaming firms while the HK entity books the transaction offshore without transfer pricing documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under IRO s.82, the partnership, partners, and responsible directors are liable to a fine of HK$100,000 plus treble the tax undercharged; under s.82A, fraudulent evasion carries imprisonment for up to 10 years; the IRD may also reopen assessments without time limits when fraud or wilful neglect is established
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced if the court finds the partner-directors used the FIP as a mere façade; each director may be jointly and severally liable for the full tax arrears, civil restitution of diverted profits, forfeiture of business assets, a HK travel restriction order under the protection of revenue provisions, and an imprisonment term of 3 to 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the HK Foreign-Invested Partnership as a zero-substance mailbox entity claiming China-HK DTA treaty benefits on passive income or licensing fees without performing CIGA in Hong Kong; Chinese gaming customers pay royalty payments to the HK FIP that actually originates in China, while the HK entity simply routes funds to ultimate shareholders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under China’s General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the China-HK arrangement’s Limitation on Benefits provisions, the tax authorities may deny treaty benefits, impose a 10% withholding under China CIT law (or higher domestic withholding if no treaty), levy late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and impose a penalty of 0.5 to 5 times the tax originally underpaid under Article 63 of the Chinese Tax Collection Law; in Hong Kong, the IRD may revoke the TRC and assess all deemed HK-source profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute offshore payment flows through a shell FIP may be personally liable under common law conspiracy involving tax fraud; courts can pierce the veil to hold directors personally for the entire underpaid tax plus statutory surcharges; directors can be blacklisted from leaving Hong Kong and China, have their assets frozen, and face criminal imprisonment of up to 7 years for fraudulent tax evasion under the joint HK-China mutual legal assistance framework

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare a Local File / Master File or failing to apply the arm’s length principle when the FIP transacts with its Chinese parent and related gaming software licensors, leading to artificial shifting of profits out of China to the lower-tax HK entity by understating royalties or service fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Hong Kong’s Inland Revenue Ordinance (Amendment) No. 6 of 2017 imposes penalties for failure to maintain adequate transfer pricing documentation: a default penalty of HK$50,000 upon first conviction and HK$5,000 per month of continuing default; the IRD may adjust the taxpayer’s profits and assess additional profits tax up to 16.5% of the adjusted amounts; China may correspondingly adjust its taxation and impose penalties under the Chinese Transfer Pricing Rules and Article 44 of the Tax Collection Law for failure to provide contemporaneous documentation, ranging from 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where documentation failure is part of a deliberate scheme to divert profits, the directors can be personally assessed under s.82A for fraudulent purposes; the corporate veil can be pierced, rendering directors personally liable for aggregate unpaid tax, penalties, and sanctions of up to treble the diverted tax; criminal penalties for individual officers include imprisonment of up to 5 years, and the directors may be personally blacklisted and subjected to HK Immigration Department travel prohibitions
